description: The graph illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (%) and the number of child nodes (tree width) for two large vision-language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, on a reasoning task. The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)," ranges from 1 to 7, with data points plotted at intervals of 2. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)," spans from 15% to 35%, with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Two lines are plotted: a solid blue line with circular markers for GPT-4o and a dashed light blue line with star markers for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. For GPT-4o, the accuracy starts at 24.4% at a tree width of 1, increases to 28.9% at 3, peaks at 34.4% at 5, and then decreases to 31.1% at 7. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, the accuracy begins at 26.7% at a tree width of 1, decreases to 27.8% at 3, then continues to decline to 24.4% at 5, and finally reaches 20.0% at 7. This shows that GPT-4o's performance follows an inverted U-shape, peaking at a tree width of 5, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet's performance monotonically decreases with increasing tree width.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
